Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.

In the heart of France, where the Eiffel Tower pierces the sky and the Seine River flows gently, a woman of unwavering dedication and passion has made a name for herself in the world of politics. Born and raised in the picturesque city of Lyon, Manuela's fascination with politics began at a young age. Growing up in a family of modest means, she witnessed firsthand the impact of government policies on everyday lives. Her parents, both hardworking individuals, struggled to make ends meet, and Manuela saw how the lack of effective representation in their community exacerbated their difficulties. This sparked a fire within her, and she vowed to make a difference. Manuela's journey into politics began with grassroots activism. She volunteered at local community centers, working closely with residents to address their concerns and develop solutions to the challenges they faced. Her tireless efforts did not go unnoticed, and soon she was approached by local party leaders to run for a seat on the city council. In 2008, Manuela Pereira was elected to the Lyon City Council, marking the beginning of her illustrious political career. As a councilor, Manuela championed causes close to her heart, including education reform, affordable housing, and environmental sustainability. Her dedication to these issues earned her the respect of her constituents and her peers. In 2012, she was re-elected with an overwhelming majority, a testament to her ability to connect with the people she represented. Manuela's success at the local level caught the attention of national party leaders, who saw in her a rising star with a deep understanding of the needs of the French people. In 2017, she was appointed as a member of the French National Assembly, representing the 7th constituency of Lyon. This marked a significant milestone in her career, as she became one of the few women of Portuguese descent to hold a seat in the National Assembly. As a member of the National Assembly, Manuela has continued to advocate for the rights of marginalized communities and push for policies that promote social justice and equality. Her work on the Committee on Cultural Affairs and Education has been instrumental in shaping the country's education policy, ensuring that every child, regardless of their background, has access to quality education.
